observations.metric_definition: National cumulative production of room air conditioners, refrigerators and washing machines for January–September 2018, as reported by MIIT from National Bureau of Statistics data.
observations.value: Room air conditioners 160.114 million units (+12.9% YoY); refrigerators 60.167 million (+2.1%); washing machines 51.471 million (+0.7%).
observations.statement: The industry entered late 2018 with materially faster room-air-conditioner production than refrigerator and washing-machine production.
observations.economic_interpretation: The common environment was not a uniform white-goods volume path: category mix and capacity/utilisation exposure could differ before any company-specific conclusion is drawn.
observations.profit_pool_effect: Higher room-air-conditioner production can support system throughput, but it does not by itself establish domestic sell-out, pricing power or issuer margin capture.
observations.permitted_inference: Use only to test whether a company's product/category exposure plausibly differed from the aggregate white-goods production backdrop.

observations.metric_definition: Aggregate home-appliance industry production-sales rate, export delivery value, operating revenue and profit for January–September 2018.
observations.value: Production-sales rate 96.6% (-1.5 percentage points YoY); export delivery RMB295.92bn (+5.9%); industry revenue RMB1,110.82bn (+11.9%) and profit RMB87.95bn (+20.3%).
observations.statement: Aggregate appliance revenue and profit grew while the production-sales rate was below the prior-year level.
observations.economic_interpretation: A growing aggregate profit pool can coexist with absorption/friction risk; the future industry thesis must distinguish aggregate accounting growth from company-level sell-through, inventory and cash conversion.
observations.profit_pool_effect: Aggregate profitability was supportive, but a weaker production-sales rate preserves a rival explanation of uneven channel absorption or category/company divergence.
observations.permitted_inference: Use to require company-level evidence on how aggregate profit-pool conditions passed through product mix, channels, working capital and cash.

observations.metric_definition: Retail sales of household appliances and audio-visual equipment at above-designated-size units, and physical-goods online retail, January–November 2018.
observations.value: Household appliances and audio-visual equipment retail RMB796.5bn (+8.3% YoY); physical-goods online retail RMB6,271.0bn (+25.4%), 18.2% of total retail sales.

observations.statement: Broad appliance retail was growing and online physical-goods retail expanded faster in the same period.
observations.economic_interpretation: The demand/channel backdrop was supportive in aggregate but channel migration could distribute its benefit unequally across companies and categories.
observations.profit_pool_effect: Broad retail growth does not settle product demand, company sell-out or price capture; it makes company-specific channel and category transmission a discriminating research question.
observations.permitted_inference: Use to compare a company's disclosed channel and category exposure against broad retail and online-channel context, not as company demand evidence.

observations.metric_definition: The 2016 national energy-efficiency-label product catalogue and implementation rules covering named household-appliance categories.
observations.period: 2016 catalogue announced on 2016-06-24; the announcement states the listed refrigerator, room-air-conditioner and washing-machine rules take effect on 2016-10-01.
observations.value: The 2016 product catalogue and implementation rules include household refrigerators, room air conditioners and electric washing machines, among other categories.
observations.statement: The Pack's principal household-appliance categories were within a common energy-efficiency-label product regime before the Pack cutoff.
observations.economic_interpretation: The category-specific label regime can affect the product/mix and channel questions that must be verified at company level, but the published catalogue alone does not measure a company's costs, product mix or customer response.
observations.profit_pool_effect: The regulation is a common product constraint and a source of possible differentiation, not evidence that any issuer captured a margin or demand advantage.
observations.permitted_inference: Require target-company verification of the relevant product scope, compliance, mix and economics when a company thesis relies on efficiency positioning.
